explanation: The sign of each trig value is just the sign of a coordinate: cos θ follows the x-coordinate and sin θ follows the y-coordinate, while tan θ = sin/cos. The deg slider sweeps the ray around all four quadrants; the dashed blue (x) and green (y) legs flip sign as the point crosses an axis, and the readout shows the resulting +/− pattern. That pattern is the ASTC rule — All positive in QI, then only Sin, then only Tan, then only Cos as you go counterclockwise.
bullets: cos θ has the sign of x; sin θ has the sign of y; tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.
ASTC: QI all +, QII sin +, QIII tan +, QIV cos + (counterclockwise).
Crossing an axis flips exactly one coordinate, flipping the matching ratios.
